text:
maria: Quick head's up — I ran a "coinflip prefill" sweep on the new quant build (llama3-70b-8q) to get a stressy worst-case for speculative prefill. Posting short notes + logs. TL;DR: ~2.8% speculative misfires, ~18% p50 latency win when speculative path taken. Need eyes before we consider a canary.

kevin: Nice. quick Q: what's your exact coinflip protocol again? remind me the steps so I don't misinterpret the numbers.

maria: Super short: for each request we randomly replace the next K tokens with uniform draws over vocab (i.e., coinflip prefill) then run speculative decode as if the model had produced those tokens. This simulates high-entropy prefixes so we can measure (a) whether speculative guesses match the final decode, (b) how often we need to fall back, (c) end-to-end latency/throughput impact.

anya: Can you paste the CLI you ran + the aggregated numbers? would help for reproducibility.

maria: Sure — command used and aggregate csv below.

```
# simplified run command
runtest --model=llama3-70b-8q --quant=8q --prefill=coinflip --K=16 --seed=42 --concurrency=200 --samples=10000 --entropy-gate=0.0
```

results.csv (cols: cohort,misfire_pct,p50_ms,p95_ms,quality_delta_pct)
```
coinflip_all,2.82,31,98,-0.9
baseline_no_spec,0.00,38,120,0.0
entropy_gate_0.3,1.12,34,105,-0.4
```

maria: notes: quality_delta measured as relative EM/accuracy on our mixed eval set; the -0.9% skew is mostly on the code subset where token boundaries are brittle.

eval-bot: AUTO: run-id=2026-06-10-coinflip-42, samples=10000, failures=282, avg_p50_baseline=38ms, avg_p50_spec=31ms, quality_delta=-0.9%, comments="misfires concentrated on code-gen, ~30% of misfires require long-rollbacks"

sam: What is the eval-set split? code vs natural language? and are fallbacks costly because of kv-cache rebuilds?

maria: Eval set: ~60% commonsense/QA, ~40% code snippets (short functions, docstring->impl). Fall-back cost: often we need to re-run from last confirmed token which triggers ~15-40ms extra compute depending on window size; larger windows are worse because of recompute on GPU kernels — that's where much of p95 hits live.

kevin: Did you try entropy gating (i.e., only spec when model's next-token entropy < threshold) or adaptive gating?

maria: Quick ablation above with entropy_gate=0.3. Lowering gating reduced misfires to 1.12% but p50 improvement dropped to ~10% (34ms vs 38ms). So gating is effective but reduces wins. Also tried a cheap heuristic: only speculative for non-code routes (based on intent tag). That keeps misfires low for code.

anya: Any regressions in safety / hallucination metrics? we need to be careful rolling this out across customer routes.

maria: Quick scan — no systemic safety flips in our small sample. Most regressions are syntactic/tokenization edgecases in code (missing braces, truncated identifiers) rather than hallucinated facts.

sam: Proposed next steps:
- Add a small canary: enable coinflip-prefill speculative for 10% of chat routes (non-code), monitor misfires & UX metrics for 48h.
- Add a targeted code holdout: block speculative path entirely for codegen model route until more checks.
- Collect per-token entropy histograms (for incoming requests) to tune gate.

kevin: Agreed. also add an ops check: measure KV-cache recompute time distribution per model-version — we might optimize kernel warmup to lower fallback cost.

maria: Will open a PR with the run artifacts, raw logs, and script to re-run. naming: repo/tests/coinflip_prefill/ — includes notebook summary.

anya: Sounds good. one more ask: can we re-run with K=32 and concurrency=500 to see tail behavior? coinflip with longer prefill probably raises misfires nonlinearly.

maria: Yep scheduling that overnight. I'll post updated csv tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks — tagging @eng-releases for rollout considerations and @security for quick sanity check.

kevin: Nice investigation. If the overnight run shows similar % misfires but stronger p50 wins, I'm in favor of a phased roll.

maria: Cool. will post follow-up. end of thread for now (saving artifacts to s3://redwood-experiments/coinflip/1777777770/)
